title: What You Are Going To Do

sections.title: What You Are Going To Do
sections.content: Spanish has a future tense, and hardly uses it in conversation. For plans it uses 'ir a' plus an infinitive — exactly like English 'going to'. You met 'ir' in Lesson 11; put 'a' after it and any verb behind that, and you can talk about everything you intend to do. The 'a' is never optional: 'voy a visitar', never 'voy visitar'.

sections.title: ir a + infinitive
rows: he, she is going to prepare

items.spanish: ¿Qué vamos a hacer durante las vacaciones?
items.english: What are we going to do during the holidays?
We're going to visit Ninh Binh.

items.spanish: Daniela va a llevar su cámara para hacer muchas fotos.
items.english: Daniela is going to take her camera to get lots of photos.

items.spanish: Creo que va a ser un viaje fantástico.
items.english: I think it's going to be a fantastic trip.

sections.content: The same 'va a' covers a prediction as well as a plan: 'va a llover' from Lesson 14 is the weather doing the going. If you can say it with 'going to' in English, this is the structure.
